about.title: Personal Injury Help in Napa, California
about.longDescription: Napa is home to about 80,000 people, and the public record tells a fuller story than its quiet reputation suggests. In 2025, the most recent final year on file, the city logged 253 injury collisions. Those crashes left 357 people injured and took 3 lives. The corridors that appear most often in the counts are familiar to anyone who lives here: Jefferson Street, Route 29, Soscol Avenue, and 1st Street through the downtown core. Reports also tend to bunch up on Thursday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., when commute and visitor traffic overlap. If one of those numbers is you, the paperwork can feel heavier than the injury itself. That is where we come in. We handle personal injury claims in Napa County. We will work with you to understand what happened and help you decide your next step. We work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most injury claims two years to be filed, and that clock is already running. A short conversation now costs nothing and keeps your options open.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Napa Claim

items.title: Two Years, Sometimes Less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, the window to give notice can shrink to as little as six months.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not Close the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. Even if you share some of the blame, your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than wiped out.

items.title: No Arbitrary Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages such as pain, loss of enjoyment, and emotional distress. Your claim can reflect what you actually went through.

items.title: Contingency Fees Only
items.desc: We work on contingency. You pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: Where do injury crashes in Napa tend to happen?
items.answer: Public collision records show the highest counts along Jefferson Street, Route 29, Soscol Avenue, and 1st Street. Reports also cluster on Thursdays between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. These are simply where and when the numbers concentrate, and any street can be the site of a crash.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, the deadline is two years from the date of the injury. Claims against a government entity, such as a city bus or a poorly maintained public sidewalk, can require notice within six months. Because those deadlines are firm, it helps to speak with an attorney early.

items.question: What if the other driver says the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so sharing blame does not bar you from recovering. Your compensation is reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you. Insurers sometimes overstate a victim's share, which is one reason people choose to have an attorney review the facts.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact us?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review. We work on contingency, which means there is no attorney fee unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: Should I talk to the insurance company before I talk to an attorney?
items.answer: You are generally required to report the crash to your own insurer, but you are not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other driver's company right away. Anything you say can be used to shape how fault or injuries are viewed. Many people prefer to get a free consultation first so they understand their position.
